_comment: Registry behind knownBug(id, ...) in support/fixtures.ts. status open: the test is expected to fail (test.fail) and turns red the day the product is fixed, then set it to fixed. status fixed: the marker is inert and the test is a regression guard. Open entries carry test, steps, expected, actual, evidence and fix. Run with E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 to see the raw failures of the open ones.

BUG-01.title: Logout does not revoke the session server-side and keeps studio hub connections open (GAP-04b)

BUG-02.title: GET /api/system/info answers anonymously and anonymous POST /api/auth/logout answers 204 (route policy matrix, GAP-04a)

BUG-03.title: A request without the X-Output-Key header answers 400 instead of the uniform 403 (GAP-06)

BUG-04.title: Credential-bearing responses (livekit-token, redeem, pairing poll) lack Cache-Control: no-store

BUG-05.title: LiveKit webhook answers 415 for Content-Type application/json (plan expects 200; LiveKit itself sends application/webhook+json)
BUG-05.steps: POST /api/livekit/webhook on the direct API port with a correctly signed body (Authorization: signed token, sha256 claim) and Content-Type: application/json.
BUG-05.actual: 415 Unsupported Media Type. The running system is not affected because LiveKit sends application/webhook+json.
BUG-05.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run of the test: 'expect(response.status).toBe(200)' received 415.
BUG-05.fix: Accept application/json next to application/webhook+json for the webhook endpoint, or change the plan.

BUG-06.title: Releasing an unknown slot answers 204 and a phone may release its only camera slot (GAP-19)

BUG-07.title: The loser of a double approve gets 410 instead of 404 (GAP-09)

BUG-08.title: An unknown enum text (kind: tablet) is a 400 without the errors object naming the field
BUG-08.expected: 400 validation_failed with an errors object that names 'kind' (numeric range errors do).
BUG-08.actual: 400 validation_failed without errors: the body binding fails before the validation runs.
BUG-08.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run: Object.keys(result.body.errors ?? {}) does not contain 'kind'.
BUG-08.fix: Map the JSON enum conversion error to the same errors shape (field name, German message).

BUG-09.title: The device kind comes from the request body, not from the invite kind (GAP-19)

BUG-10.title: Log texts of block/unblock/remove contain the device name («K1 Handy 1 gesperrt»); prototype and plan have «K1 gesperrt»
BUG-10.steps: Pair a phone named «Handy 1» (code K1); block it, then unblock it; read the logAppended events.
BUG-10.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run: expected 'K1 gesperrt', received 'K1 Handy 1 gesperrt'.
BUG-10.fix: Cosmetic. Either drop the name from the texts or change the prototype and the plan.

BUG-11.title: Pending knock requests survive the activation of another production (GAP-36)

BUG-12.title: Image dimension limit is 65535, not the pinned 16384; a 60000 x 60000 header is accepted (GAP-13)

BUG-13.title: Asset content without any credential answers 403 instead of 401 (GAP-13)

BUG-14.title: Asset content has no ETag; If-Range with a non-matching validator still answers 206

BUG-15.title: File name sanitiser keeps U+202E and dot-only names; fallback name differs from the pinned «Medium» (UNIT-MEDIA-01)

BUG-16.title: HEAD on the asset content endpoint answers 405
BUG-16.steps: Upload a PNG, then HEAD /api/productions/{id}/assets/{asset}/content?k={output key}.
BUG-16.expected: 200 with the headers of GET (Content-Type image/png, nosniff) and no body (INT-MEDIA-06, E2E-AUTH-17).
BUG-16.actual: 405 Method Not Allowed: only GET is mapped.
BUG-16.fix: Map HEAD next to GET (MapMethods) for the content endpoint.

BUG-18.title: X-Content-Type-Options is sent twice on API responses (API and Caddy both add it)
BUG-18.steps: GET /api/auth/me through Caddy with a valid session and read all x-content-type-options headers.
BUG-18.actual: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, nosniff - the API middleware and the Caddyfile (base_headers) both add it.
BUG-18.fix: Keep one of the two (e.g. header ?X-Content-Type-Options in Caddy, or remove the API's).

BUG-19.title: Device reports are relayed to the Regie as telemetry at once (no 2 s throttle per device)
BUG-19.steps: Regie hub subscribed; a paired phone's device hub calls ReportLive(['camera']) every 100 ms for 8 s.
BUG-19.expected: At most one 'telemetry' message per device and 2 s (spec 6, INT-SYNC-05, INT-SRC-03): at most 6 messages in 8 s, never closer than 1.7 s.
BUG-19.actual: Every report is relayed at once: 92 messages in 10 s for 10 reports/s.
BUG-19.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run 2026-10-22: 'relayed 74 messages in 8 s' (limit 6); an earlier run counted 92 in 10 s. The sender stand-in reports once a second, so even real phones cause one message per second each.
BUG-19.fix: Relay the first report at once, then at most one per device and 2 s (keep the newest in between).

BUG-20.title: A graceful API shutdown (docker restart / compose restart / update) writes a «K1 verbindet neu» log entry for every source in Program or Preview although the restart is no outage of the source (UNIT-SRC-03: such entries must not appear)
BUG-20.steps: Pair a phone whose camera slot is live and in the program scene (hub reports every second); docker restart api; the phone reconnects (Hello, ReportLive) once the API is back; wait beyond SOURCES__RESTARTGRACE (15 s).
BUG-20.expected: No incidentUpserted and no log entry «verbindet neu» for the restart; the source is offline while the hub is away and ok when it is back (UNIT-SRC-03, E2E-LK-03).
BUG-20.actual: About 200 ms after the restart begins (during the graceful shutdown) the log gets «K1 verbindet neu»; it is persisted and still in recentLog after the restart. Probe: before status=ok log=['K1 Probe gekoppelt']; +2.2 s status=offline log=['K1 verbindet neu@13:08:38.431', ...]; later status=ok, incidents=0. A kill/crash path (no shutdown handler) writes no entry.
BUG-20.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run: added log entries ['K2 verbindet neu', 'K1 verbindet neu'] for two phones.
BUG-20.fix: Do not run the source-loss path for hub disconnects caused by the host stopping (IHostApplicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping), or suppress the log entry then.

BUG-21.title: With PostgreSQL stopped, every request that needs the database (reads, writes, the login) hangs for 16-46 s before the API answers 503 ProblemDetails; through Caddy the user gets a plain-text 504 Gateway Timeout after 30 s instead, so the Regie has no error to show during a 30 s outage (GAP-32)
BUG-21.test: E2E-NET-11 [stack, latency] (specs/net/net-resilience.disruptive.spec.ts); E2E-NET-11 [stack] passes and records the API's own answer.
BUG-21.steps: docker compose stop postgres; at once GET /api/productions/{id}/snapshot, PATCH a scene and POST /api/auth/login (direct port and through Caddy); then start postgres again.
BUG-21.expected: /health/ready 503 within 5 s and /health/live 200; reads and writes answer 503 ProblemDetails (no stack, no connection string) so the Regie can show an error toast within seconds (INT-NET-04, E2E-NET-11).
BUG-21.actual: /health/ready 503 after 4.0 s and /health/live 200 (correct). The API answers 503 ProblemDetails (title «Vorübergehend nicht verfügbar», no leak) only after 42.3 s (read), 46.1 s (list) and 46.1 s (login) on the direct port. Through Caddy one run got a plain-text '504 Gateway Timeout' (response_header_timeout 60s), another the 503 after 16.6 s. After PostgreSQL returns, readiness is 200 again after about 2 s without restarting the API (correct).
BUG-21.evidence: Direct-port probe at the time of the finding: ready 503 4001 ms; live 200 2 ms; GET snapshot 503 42254 ms; GET productions 503 46080 ms; POST login 503 46082 ms; ready again 1951 ms after start. The latency test through Caddy measured the 503 after 16.6 s and 27.1 s in two runs and a plain '504 Gateway Timeout' in a third; with three requests at once on the direct port (run 3, 30 s outage plus recovery wait): read answered after 126.8 s, login after 50.0 s and the write had no answer at all after 150 s (E2E-NET-11 [stack] records such cases as 'unanswered'); the latency test measured 20.4 s through Caddy in that run.
BUG-21.fix: Shorten the database connection and command timeouts for request handling (for example Timeout=2;Command Timeout=5 in the connection string, or a request-level cancellation) so the 503 arrives within about 5 s.

BUG-22.title: The postgres service has no cap_drop: ALL (caddy, api and livekit have it); E2E-OPS-01 and -13 require it for every service
BUG-22.steps: docker compose config --format json (production file) and docker inspect of the running postgres container.
BUG-22.expected: cap_drop: [ALL] / HostConfig.CapDrop contains ALL for every service (E2E-OPS-01, E2E-OPS-13).
BUG-22.actual: postgres: cap_drop is empty (Docker's default capability set). caddy, api and livekit have ALL.
BUG-22.evidence: E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 run: 'postgres cap_drop in docker-compose.yml' received [].
BUG-22.fix: cap_drop: [ALL] plus cap_add: [CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID] for the official image entrypoint; verify first start, restart and restore.sh afterwards.

DOC-01.title: docs/testing.md pins microphone=() for /join/*; implementation-spec section 10 and the Caddyfile have microphone=(self)

DOC-02.title: Event order of a redeem differs from the order pinned in INT-PAIR-01: the API emits inviteRemoved first and the replacement inviteUpserted last (no functional impact)

DOC-03.title: docs/testing.md pins a LiveKit participant token lifetime of 2 h; implementation-spec section 7 and the API use 10 minutes (the tests assert the implementation-spec value)

DOC-04.title: docs/testing.md E2E-OPS-06 and E2E-NET-13 use docker kill to simulate a crash; since Docker 29 a killed container is counted as manually stopped and the restart policy does not bring it back (verified: plain alpine container, restart unless-stopped and always, Docker 29.8.2). The suite crashes services with kill -TERM 1 (-QUIT for PostgreSQL) inside the container (dockerCtl.crash)

DOC-07.title: docs/testing.md E2E-OPS-05 degrades a service with docker pause and expects unhealthy within interval x retries; Docker 29.8.2 marks a paused container unhealthy at once, even for a check that is just 'true' (control container), so the method cannot show that a check exercises the service. The suite adds [command] tests: the check runs in the container (exit 0) and in a container of the same image without the service (exit != 0)

OBS-01.title: Graceful shutdown of the API with connected hub clients is slow and erratic: 0.6 s without clients, 1.6-7 s in some runs, but 31-32 s (the 30 s default HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout) in others; once docker compose restart api needed 59.8 s on a loaded machine
OBS-01.test: E2E-NET-12 [api] restart and crash (specs/net/net-resilience.disruptive.spec.ts); no separate failing test because the duration is not deterministic
OBS-01.steps: Five hub clients connected (two Regie, one output, two phones) through Caddy; SIGTERM to the API (kill -TERM 1 inside the container, or docker compose restart api); measure until the container is healthy again.
OBS-01.expected: T-RESTART-API: docker restart api -> healthy within 30 s (hard), hubs closed at once (INT-NET-05) so a restart takes a few seconds.
OBS-01.actual: crash variant: 32.2 s, 32.2 s, 32.2 s, 32.3 s, 32.3 s (five repetitions); probe with four clients: 7.0 s, 4.1 s (restart), 31.0 s; probe with three clients: 1.6 s; run without clients: 0.6 s. docker compose restart api: 2.5-5.4 s in nine runs, 59.8 s in one (the restart test failed its 30 s limit once in 7 full-run observations). The 30 s plateau is the default ShutdownTimeout, i.e. something (a hub connection or a hosted service) does not stop in time.
OBS-01.evidence: annotations 'crash: container back and healthy after 32290 ms' / 'restart: ... 59829 ms' in the JSON report of the full run; probe timings above.
OBS-01.fix: Find what keeps StopAsync waiting (log at Debug the hosted services and connections that are still open when ApplicationStopping fires); abort hub connections on ApplicationStopping and set an explicit HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout of about 5 s. update.sh / compose recreate stops the API with Docker's 10 s grace and then SIGKILLs it.

DOC-06.title: docs/testing.md UNIT-SRC-01 / INT-SRC-03 / E2E-SRC pin slot state paused = ended; implementation-spec 4.5 (decided 2026-10-22, still uncommitted) makes paused = the OS suspended the capture = reconnecting, ended = stopped on purpose, and replaces slot states per report / per session. The tests follow the implementation spec

DOC-05.title: docs/testing.md E2E-OPS-02 lists an empty domain as invalid input; setup.sh uses the node IP as the domain in internal mode (its prompt says so), with a public TLS mode it is an error
